title: fix(app-shell): a member who may read none of an app's objects lands on one access page
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoL6oH8EmKk5FD1KRSQUD9wm)_

Part of objectstack-ai/objectstack#25338

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

A member who may read none of the objects an app names landed on the app's dashboard (the object-read prune only drops `type: 'object'` entries, so the dashboard entry survived) and saw a grid of "You don't have access" tiles. The app root's landing now asks the prune's own verdict, `useNavMemberGates().can`, over every object entry the app names, at every depth and in every area. When the app names at least one object and the member may read none of them, it renders the existing `AppNoAccessEmptyState` (objectui#12079) with a new `reason="no-readable-object"`:

> Your account cannot read any of the records in this app yet. Ask an administrator to assign you a permission set.

A member who may grant access also gets the Setup link, as with the no-navigation reason. One readable object, or an app that names no object at all, lands exactly as before.

- `appServesNoNavigation.ts`: new pure predicate `appNamesOnlyUnreadableObjects(app, can)`.
- `AppNoAccessEmptyState.tsx`: `reason` prop (default `no-navigation`, unchanged copy), `data-reason` on the description.
- `AppContent.tsx` `AppRootLanding`: one early return before the landing is chosen. No hooks follow it. `can` never answers for a pending read, because `MePermissionsProvider` renders its fallback until it holds an answer.
- `@object-ui/i18n`: two keys in all 10 locales.

The companion objectstack PR (same branch name) lets Create User grant a permission set in the same step, so an administrator can avoid this state in the first place.

## Verification

- New `AppContent.noReadableObjectLanding-25338.test.tsx`, 4/4: none readable gives the empty state at `/apps/crm`; one readable lands on the dashboard; an app naming no object lands on the dashboard; an object named only under `areas` that is readable lands on the dashboard.
- Ablation: with the guard disabled (`if (false && …)`), the first case goes red ("may read none of the named objects: the app-level empty state, not the dashboard"); restored, green.
- `AppContent.*`, `AppNoAccess*` and `packages/i18n` tests: 115 files, 1556 passed, 13 skipped.
- Root gates: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:vi-mock-*` (3), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources` all exit 0. eslint on the changed files: 0 errors.
- Not run here: `app-shell` `type-check` (this checkout has no built `@object-ui/*` dist, so every workspace import is unresolved; no error is in the changed lines beyond that) and `check:eager-locale-catalogues` (needs a built console bundle). CI covers both.

## Out of scope

"Whom to ask" is the generic "an administrator": the app carries no owner or contact field to name a person.
